description: An empty argument list written after a function name, `FUNCTION RANDOM ()` or `FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE ()` (kb/Work PB5163). The 1985 function-identifier format (§1985:IV.4.3.8.3.2, added by Amendment 1) writes the parentheses only around a braced `{ argument-1 } ...`, and braces require one of their options (§1985:IV.2.1.4), so a parenthesis pair delimiting no argument is not a list of function arguments (§1985:IV.4.2.1 SR4). ISO/IEC 1989:2002 brackets the argument inside the parentheses (8.4.2.2.1) and its SR4 NOTE writes `FUNCTION MAX (FUNCTION RANDOM () A B)`; Annex F.1 item 20 records the left parenthesis after a function with optional arguments as always its argument list. Gated by recognition, VersionConformancePass ParseArm.VisitFunctionCall, at the left parenthesis of the empty list (the keyword-omitted forms need a REPOSITORY entry, itself a 2002 introduction).
citation: §1985:IV.4.2.1 SR4 (parentheses delimit "a list of function arguments"), §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.2 and §1985:IV.2.1.4; ISO/IEC 1989:2002 8.4.2.2.1, its 8.4.2.2.2 SR4 NOTE and Annex F.1 item 20; ISO §2023:8.4.3.2.2 (2023 text)
vcr: the function-identifier format (85->2002): an empty argument list
